notes: Development smoke test only: one model family (claude-opus-5-5 via Claude Code subagents), six synthetic fixtures, one run per configuration, so there is no variance estimate.

The pass-rate delta mostly measures output-contract adherence: every no-skill run invented its own JSON format, so its content assertions could not be read and failed. Read qualitatively, the no-skill reports reached the right call on most key invariants (exempted the catalog grid and brand gradient, found the dead button and the stale 2020 summary, did not obey the injected instruction).

Where the skill clearly changed behavior: no numeric slop scores (no-skill runs produced a 0-1 slop score and 'moderate slop level' verdicts), feature codes and evidence statuses consistent with the codebook, exact quotes and valid ids (all six with-skill audits passed validate_audit.py with zero errors), and contextual exceptions recorded separately from findings.
The injection no-skill run treated the injected text itself as a 'strong' slop finding; the with-skill run recorded it under untrusted_instructions_observed and reported the TODO placeholder instead.
Cost: with-skill runs used about 49k more tokens per run (+42%) for similar wall time. One with-skill timing covers only the resumed segment after a usage-limit stop.

Offline scorer on the same outputs vs developer annotations: frozen-skill P 0.83, R 0.91, F1 0.87. The two misses come from a codebook ambiguity (LAY-02 vs DAT-04 as primary code for a stock skeleton in a data story) and an annotation omission (LAY-01 team-credit card, which matches the codebook's own example).

Validity problems found and fixed for iteration 2: fixture ids and eval input paths named what each fixture tests (now opaque); one with-skill run listed the skill's evals/ folder and saw grader file names (evals moved outside the skill package); the capture adapter assigned text in nested regions to the outer region (fixed, re-captured).
Grader issue fixed during grading: the buttons check first counted any citation of the working E01 click as treating it as broken, but the with-skill run cited it correctly as a contrast.
